trace.final_message:
Added `hourglass/rounding.py` with `rounded_labels(spans, step)`. It snaps each start and end to the nearest step and returns one label per span, in input order. Each label is the start-end range followed by the length in hours and minutes, so a range from nine o'clock to a quarter past five reads with an eight hour fifteen minute length.

Choices I made that you may want to change:
- The step must be a positive divisor of sixty. Zero, negative, or uneven steps raise `ValueError` before any span is processed.
- Exact halves round up, so a span edge exactly between two steps moves forward.
- A span that collapses to nothing after rounding raises `ValueError` instead of being dropped, so no shift disappears from payroll. If payroll would rather see a zero-length label, that is a small change.
- The length always shows minutes, so a whole hour still shows a zero minute part.
- I did not add the function to the package exports in `hourglass/__init__.py`. Import it from `hourglass.rounding`.

I also added a line to the Unreleased section of `CHANGES.txt` and to `docs/api.txt`.

Tests are in `tests/test_rounding.py` and cover step validation, rounding, labels, and the end-of-day edge. `make check` runs thirty-eight tests, all passing: the twenty-six existing tests and twelve new ones. `make lint` reports no syntax errors.

Committed on `master` with the subject "Add rounded_labels for snapping spans to a clock step" and the Co-Authored-By trailer. `master` is the current branch, and `main` is the default branch, so the commit is not on `main` yet.

commits.message:
Add rounded_labels for snapping spans to a clock step

Rounds each start and end of a span to the nearest step and returns a label
such as 09:00-17:15 (8h 15m). The step must be a positive divisor of an hour;
anything else raises ValueError. A span that collapses to nothing after
rounding also raises, so no shift silently disappears from payroll.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

before.CHANGES.txt:
## Unreleased
- Clearer wording when a span ends before it starts.

## 0.7.1 (2026-07-08)
- normalize_day accepts full day names in any case.

## 0.7.0 (2026-04-22)
- Add format_day_line and day_coverage.
- worker_minutes no longer merges overlaps for the same worker.

## 0.6.0 (2025-12-15)
- Read schedules from CSV.

## 0.5.0 (2025-09-30)
- Add intersect_spans. Touching spans no longer count as overlapping.
before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
